findings.title: Gating-equivalence case label misdescribed its body
findings.action: Rename the case after its body
findings.disposition_rationale: 77ca534f renamed it to 'fault: claim bullet empty, next bullet follows directly'.

findings.title: Two-sided number stripping bound anchors the spec keeps undefended
findings.action: Restore the spec's one-sided rule and pin that a wrong or missing section number stays undefended
findings.disposition_rationale: 877c7b7e reverted 821a2896 (library code is byte-identical to 77ca534f); dbadc5c8 pins '2-out-of-scope' against '## Out of scope' and '## 8. Out of scope' as undefended.

findings.title: require() inside an ESM test file throws
findings.disposition_rationale: The file defines require via createRequire(import.meta.url) at line 12; the test runs and passes (47/47).

findings.title: case_file_anchor stores the numbered slug, so a renumbered spec loses the binding on redispatch
findings.action: Strip the number on both sides
findings.disposition_rationale: Behaviour the spec chose: section 4 stores the bound slug so a re-derive hits the exact arm, and a heading that later disappears gives anchor-lost on redispatch. Stripping both sides (tried in 821a2896) binds wrong-number anchors the spec keeps undefended, so it was reverted; a re-bind-on-renumber rule would need a spec amendment.

findings.title: The pre-change digest constant is an unverifiable trust-me value
findings.disposition_rationale: Phase 1 ran the new test file against the origin/main modules: the digest test passes there, so the constant was captured from pre-change behaviour.

findings.title: The number-prefix fallback can defend a fabricated anchor by slug coincidence
findings.action: None needed; recorded as an accepted residual
findings.disposition_rationale: The bound text is always the orchestrator's own spec section and the match must be unique; the spec-review infosec lens weighed the same trust surface as a residual, not an exploit path.
